scope: CFG aggregation, mixed causal ownership and correction scope only; not final workflow/online acceptance
method: Read source/test text and parse existing XML using pinned Python standard library only; no project imports, tests, compiler/backend calls, model calls, Skills or replay; only these new reports were written.

checks.conclusion: Wire and canonical schemas must pass before compiler diagnosis. Safe preflight errors and all compiler diagnostics are concatenated; owner indices are shifted by the exact preflight count. Compiler success cannot override preflight errors. No diagnostic-only partial graph is accepted.

Wire/canonical schema and source-copy barriers are explicit and force whole-response fallback. Unknown compiler exceptions propagate. The aggregation makes no claim to inspect compiler issues behind these unsafe barriers.

The producer requires exact known constructor issue text and typed ownership for every endpoint/dispatch issue. The selector checks original raw candidate digest, diagnostic owner indices, actual rejected records, every endpoint occurrence, dispatch instruction/edge identities and counts, and rederives the full surviving guarded empty-input dispatch inventory.

Actually absent endpoints, ambiguous identities, binary-dispatch/topology errors, unowned global errors and stale bindings fall back to whole correction. Allowed record merge retains exact topology and unselected records, and is followed by whole validation.

The initial reviewed selector did not bind global diagnostic text to the typed cause. Current pure v1 and mixed v2 certificates now bind exact code, normalized document path and original message digest. Changed global code/message or missing binding falls back to whole correction. This was a correction-scope integrity concern, not an observed partial-graph acceptance bypass.

limitations: Static independent review and receipt accounting do not prove future model correction success or full GA4 workflow completion.
Aggregation deliberately stops behind invalid wire/canonical schemas or unresolved source copying.
The root diagnostic digest binds recorded evidence; it is not an adversarial cryptographic authentication boundary against rewriting all artifacts.
No actual preparation, launch, new model experiment, historical validation or replay was performed.
